original_question: Is it consistent that the independence number i equals ℵ1 and that the strong polarized relation \( inom{i}{\omega} 	o  inom{i}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.10: the paper asks exactly whether it is consistent that the independence number \mathfrak{i} equals \aleph_1 and the strong polarized relation \binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega} \to \binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds. The immediately preceding sentence says that these are the problems about the independence number. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact official target almost verbatim: it has the right consistency question, the right invariant (the independence number), the right value \aleph_1, and the exact two-color strong polarized relation from Problem 3.10. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
missing_details: Use the paper's standard notation \mathfrak{i} rather than plain i, and say explicitly that \mathfrak{i} is the independence number on \omega. The paper identifies Problem 3.10 as one of the problems 'about the independence number.' ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
State that the arrow notation is the strong polarized relation, as defined in Definition 1.1. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

Unpack the relation explicitly: for every coloring c: \mathfrak{i} \times \omega \to 2, there must be A \subseteq \mathfrak{i} and B \subseteq \omega such that |A| = \mathfrak{i}, |B| = \omega, and c\upharpoonright(A \times B) is constant. This is exactly what Definition 1.1 says for \binom{\lambda}{\kappa} \to \binom{\lambda}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

Make explicit that the consistency sought is consistency with ZFC; the paper phrases the problem simply as 'Is it consistent that ... ?' in its list of open problems. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

To keep the question paper-faithful, distinguish it from the neighboring ultrafilter-number variant (Problem 3.11) and from the broader background theorem below the splitting number (Theorem 2.6); those give context but are not the target statement itself. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that the independence number \mathfrak{i} on \omega is \aleph_1 and that the strong polarized partition relation \binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega} \to \binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, for every coloring c: \mathfrak{i} \times \omega \to 2 there exist A \subseteq \mathfrak{i} and B \subseteq \omega with |A| = \mathfrak{i} = \aleph_1 and |B| = \omega such that c\upharpoonright(A \times B) is constant? ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is there a model of ZFC in which \mathfrak{i} = \aleph_1 and every 2-coloring of \mathfrak{i} \times \omega contains a monochromatic rectangle A \times B with |A| = \mathfrak{i} and B infinite countable? ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 3 rather than the introductory survey results: it matches Problem 3.10 exactly, not a broader neighboring problem. Definition 1.1 supplies the needed meaning of the polarized-arrow notation, and Theorem 2.6 is the closest nearby general background result explaining the positive relation below the splitting number, but the official open problem your draft is trying to capture is still Problem 3.10 itself. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
